definition: The pieces of text from a fixed vocabulary that a language model actually reads.
A way of learning a vocabulary: start from single characters or bytes and repeatedly merge the most frequent adjacent pair.
The raw score a model gives each vocabulary entry at a position, before the softmax.
2 raised to the mean bits per token. It can be compared only between models that share a tokenizer.
The average cost -log2 p of the true next token. Bits per character compares models with different tokenizers.
A function that turns a list of scores into probabilities that add up to 1.
A table with one row of numbers per vocabulary entry; looking up a token reads its row.
One independent set of queries, keys and values within an attention layer.
Attention for one head: softmax of the query-key scores divided by the square root of the key size, plus a mask, times the values.
A head that finds an earlier occurrence of the current token and reads the token that followed it, which lets a model copy a repeated sequence.
Switching a component off to test whether it is used.
The running total every sub-layer adds to: each reads a normalised copy and writes its result back.
Normalising before each sub-layer, inside the residual branch.
The two-layer network applied to each position on its own; it holds two thirds of a block's parameters.
Applying the final layer norm and output layer to the residual stream after any block, to see the model's current guess.
Encoding position by rotating queries and keys, so the score depends only on how far apart two tokens are.
Adam with weight decay separated from the gradient update.
Raising the learning rate linearly from near zero at the start of training.
Scaling the gradient down when its norm exceeds a limit.
Sampling filters: top-k keeps the k most likely tokens, top-p keeps the smallest set whose probabilities add up to p.
A transformer layout with no mask: every token can read every token (BERT).
A transformer layout with the causal mask: a token reads only itself and earlier tokens (GPT-2).
Attention from decoder tokens to the encoder's output, so a target text can read the source.
BERT's training task: recover tokens that were hidden, using both sides.
A fitted formula for how the loss falls with parameters and data.
The split of a fixed compute budget between model size and training tokens that gives the lowest loss.
A short signature of a text's word shingles used to find near-copies without comparing every pair.
A base model trained further on conversations in a fixed chat template.
The fixed format with role markers in which a conversation is written for the model.
A model trained on pairs of preferred and rejected answers to score any answer.
Sampling N answers and keeping the one a reward model scores highest.
Direct preference optimisation: training the model on preference pairs without a separate reward model.
Freezing a weight matrix and learning a low-rank change B A that can be merged back exactly.
The loss of earlier abilities after fine-tuning, tracked here by the loss on unrelated text.
A loop in which the model decides at each step whether to call a tool or give its final answer.
The share of questions whose answer passage is among the top k retrieved.
Combining rankings by giving each passage 1 / (60 + rank) from each ranking and adding.
The keys and values each layer has already computed, kept so a decoding step processes only the new token.
Several query heads sharing one key/value head, which shrinks the KV cache.
Prefill reads the whole prompt at once; decoding writes the answer one token per step.
Storing weights as small integers times a scale, to save memory and reading time.
A small draft model proposes several tokens and the large model checks them all in one pass.
Test questions having been seen during training, which makes a benchmark score too good.
A judge's preference for an answer because of where it is shown rather than what it says.
An interval for the difference between two setups computed on the same seeds or items, which removes the shared noise.
Requiring p below 0.05 divided by the number of tests, to keep false discoveries rare.
Classifying without training on examples of the task, by comparing an input with text descriptions of the classes.
A logistic regression trained on a frozen model's vectors.
